label: t2-patterns-data
topic: Track 2 data and reproducibility: Cremer 2019 E. coli chemotactic range-expansion source data, re-analysis of the earlier agents' pilot numbers
summary: Downloaded and hashed the three source files the design leans on (Cremer 2019 Extended Data Fig 1c, ED Fig 8, simulation parameter file) plus the simulation code. They are byte-identical to the scout's copies. Three scripts run from a clean directory and a second clean run gave identical hashes and identical output. Every pilot number the scout and designer reported reproduced: k = 16.9035 mm^2/h (they wrote 16.91 and 16.907; 0.02 percent apart, input rounding); square-root-law errors on the scout's six held-out rows 10.2 to 63.9 percent (they said 10 to 64); log-log slope of speed on growth rate 1.124 (5 points) and 0.895 (4 points) vs 1.12 and 0.90; dose slopes 0.300 (glucose) and 0.282 (glycerol) vs 0.30 and 0.28; fitted chemotactic gap 0.7873 vs 0.7874 mm^2/h; published-parameter speed 4.865 mm/h, 12.2 percent above measurement (12 reported). Nothing contradicted. New findings: (a) the scout's six held-out strains omit the 8 Pu-glpFK rows; over all 14 non-fit rows the square-root law is within 15 percent on only 6 and off by up to 94 percent; (b) the 95 percent interval of the 5-point slope is 0.72 to 1.53 and of the 4-point slope 0.44 to 1.35, so the 4-point slope does not exclude exponent 0.5; 18 of 25 speed means rest on 2 or fewer plates; (c) plain Fisher-KPP speed 2 sqrt(D r) with the published D_rho is 4.7 to 5.1 times too slow for wild type, so the library's fisher-kpp-speed law (candidate in 1.8.1) is only the zero-chemotaxis baseline; (d) the design's F1 alpha window (0.47 to 0.92) reproduces. Not obtainable under the rules: the 168 MB confocal archive (over the 150 MB cap) and the swimming videos (about 110 files of 0.7 to 1.8 GB). Twelve quarantined source-data sheets were downloaded and hashed but never opened by any script, so the pre-registration blind is intact.
lay_summary: Earlier team members reported that bacteria spreading through soft jelly follow a simple speed rule that works for some strains and fails for others. We downloaded the same public measurements from the journal and redid every calculation from scratch. All the numbers they quoted came out the same, give or take rounding. We also found two things they did not say. The rule fails more often than reported once every strain is counted. And one key claim is shakier than it looks, because each data point rests on only two or three plates. A clean computer can repeat everything with one command, a bit like re-weighing a recipe's ingredients: the recipe card was right, but some weights came from very small samples.

glossary.plain: A population spreading outward into new territory, like a colony growing across a plate.
A jelly so watery that swimming bacteria can move through it.
How fast the outer edge of the colony advances, in millimetres per hour.
How fast the population multiplies per hour in a flask.
Data not used to set the rule, kept to test it.

The range that would contain the true value in 95 of 100 repeats of the experiment.

Downloaded and fingerprinted but deliberately not opened, so later predictions stay blind.
The textbook speed of a growing, randomly spreading population: twice the square root of diffusion times growth rate.

findings.claim: Source-data files MOESM11, MOESM22, MOESM3 downloaded 2026-11-12; their sha256 are identical to the scout's earlier copies.
ED Fig 1c has 25 condition rows (speed, growth rate, n); 18 of 25 speed means have n of 2 or fewer plates.
REPRODUCED k = 16.9035 mm^2/h (sum u^2 r / sum r^2 over wt rows 3-8). Scout reported 16.91, designer 16.907.
REPRODUCED per-condition u^2/r for the six wt carbon sources: 16.15, 13.70, 20.70, 18.82, 17.46, 17.86 (scout last value 17.87).
REPRODUCED held-out errors of u = sqrt(k r): Pu-ptsG1 +10.7 and +14.9 %, Pu-ptsG2 +63.9, +34.3, +10.2 %, glpK22 -17.1 %; scout said 10 to 64 percent.

NEW: the scout's six held-out strains omit the Pu-glpFK rows. Over all 14 non-fit rows the square-root law errs 7.8 to 94.0 %, and only 6 of 14 fall within 15 %. Worst: Pu-glpFK 0 uM +94 %, Pu-glpFK serine 10 uM +76.8 %.
REPRODUCED log-log slope of speed on growth rate, Pu-glpFK aspartate series: 1.124 (5 points), 0.895 (4 points, no zero-inducer). Reported 1.12 and 0.90.
NEW: 95 % CI of those slopes (OLS, t with n-2 df) is 0.717 to 1.532 (5 points) and 0.436 to 1.353 (4 points). The 4-point interval contains 0.5; the 5-point interval excludes 0.5 narrowly.
NEW: the WT six-carbon-source slope of speed on growth rate is 0.424, 95 % CI 0.133 to 0.715, consistent with 0.5.

REPRODUCED dose slopes for aspartate 10 to 100 uM (OLS on 10, 30, 50, 100): glucose 0.2998, glycerol 0.2818; two-point version 0.294 and 0.282. Reported 0.30 and 0.28. A square root would give a 3.16-fold rise from 10 to 100 uM; observed 1.97 (glucose) and 1.92 (glycerol).
Dose-series peaks: glucose at 1000 uM (4.650 mm/h; 2.104 at 10 mM), glycerol at 100 uM (3.675 mm/h; 1.317 at 10 mM); 10 and 11 points. Matches the design.
The 100 uM rows of the dose series equal the ED Fig 1c glucose and glycerol rows exactly (same numbers re-used, not independent).

Parameter file: D_chemotaxis_1 = 50.2e-12, xhi_1 = 0.315e-9, D_nutrients = 8.0e-10, weber_offset_1 = 0.001, weber_offsetmax_1 = 0.03. Units are not stated in the file; the designer's reading is m^2/s and mM, giving 50.2, 315, 800 um^2/s and 1, 30 uM.
REPRODUCED fitted gap X = chi0 - D_rho: 0.7873 mm^2/h = 218.7 um^2/s, chi0 = 268.9 um^2/s, phi = 4.357 (designer 0.7874, 218.7, 268.9, 4.36).
REPRODUCED published-parameter closed-form speed 4.865 mm/h at r = 0.9985, 12.2 % above the measured 4.335 (designer 4.87, 12 %).
REPRODUCED sensitivity d ln c / d ln D_rho at fixed phi = 0.8927 (fit) and 0.8757 (published); designer 0.893 and 0.876.
REPRODUCED F1 refutation window for alpha: 0.471 to 0.919 around s_obs = 1.12 (design: about 0.47 to 0.92). Around the 4-point slope the window would be 0.218 to 0.666.

REPRODUCED F2 e-fold lengths u/r: 4.751 mm (glycerol+asp), 4.341 (glucose+asp); F3 uptake ratios 1.395, 1.485, 2.849; F4 max/quadrature 4.20/5.58 (wt glycerol), 5.85/7.66 (glpK22), 2.01/2.77/4.17 and 2.39/3.75/5.83 (Pu-glpFK). These are arithmetic on seen rows, not tests.

NEW: Fisher-KPP c = 2 sqrt(D_rho r) with D_rho = 0.1807 mm^2/h gives 0.850 mm/h (glucose), 0.748 (glycerol), 0.626 (acetate); measured speeds are 5.10, 4.91, 4.73 times higher. Only the Pu-glpFK 0 uM strain is as low as 2.49 times.

Law set 1.8.1 pins fisher-kpp-speed 1.1.0 (candidate, introduced 1.8.0) and turing-ddi 1.1.0 (candidate, introduced 1.8.0). turing-wavelength 1.1.0 has a registry file but is not pinned (introduced_in null). No law covers chemotactic travelling fronts. The earlier mapper's id turing-ddi-linear-condition is now turing-ddi.

fisher-kpp-speed is arithmetic of c^2 = 4 s D under a stated hypothesis, not a claim that a population disperses diffusively; given the 5-fold excess speed it is the non-chemotactic baseline for this front.
findings.evidence_quote: it does not establish that a travelling wave exists, that compactly supported initial data converge to it, or that any population disperses diffusively.

key_claims.claim: Every pilot number the earlier agents reported from ED Fig 1c, ED Fig 8 and the parameter file reproduces from the freshly downloaded files (k 16.9035, slopes 1.124 and 0.895, dose slopes 0.300 and 0.282, X 0.7873, 4.865 mm/h).
The Pu-glpFK exponent evidence is statistically weak: the 4-point slope 0.895 has 95 % CI 0.44 to 1.35, which contains 0.5, and each point is a mean of 2 to 3 plates.
Aspartate dependence between 10 and 100 uM is 0.28 to 0.30, not 0.5, on both carbon sources (100/10 ratio 1.97 and 1.92 vs 3.16 for a square root).
The confocal archive needed for F2 and the density half of F3 is 168,455,158 bytes, over the 150 MB cap, so those predictions cannot be run under the rules without an exception.

State the held-out error of the square-root law over all 14 rows (6 of 14 within 15 percent), not just the scout's six.
Obtain a size exception for the 168 MB confocal archive (needed for F2 and the density half of F3), or run F2 on the MOESM12 and MOESM14 profiles after Freeze A.
Freeze A should cite the sha256 values in this file; the 12 quarantined files are already fingerprinted and unopened.
For the Lean bridge, treat fisher-kpp-speed as the zero-chemotaxis baseline, about 5 times below the measured front.
Update design text from turing-ddi-linear-condition to turing-ddi (law set 1.8.1).
